Harbour Place: streets and boundaries

items.t: Harbour Place is a slope neighbourhood around Baker Drive and King Albert Avenue, north of Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue and below Como Lake, and the City publishes no boundary for the sub-area name.
Blue Mountain Park, at 975 King Albert Avenue at the foot of Blue Mountain, is the addressed park inside the pocket, and its spray park shares the same 975 King Albert Avenue address.
Como Lake Park, at 700 Gatensbury Street just north of the houses, is the neighbourhood's lake edge, reached from Baker Drive via Como Lake Avenue.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: the housing stock

items.t: The stock on the Baker Drive and King Albert Avenue streets is house stock around a park, not a named subdivision: no City, School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) or BC Assessment public page states a subdivision name, build decade or lot size for Harbour Place.

The amenity that shapes daily life on these streets is Blue Mountain Park's summer water set: a spray park and a wading pool at 975 King Albert Avenue, listed by the City as separate facilities at the same address.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Como Lake is a protected headwater, not just a view: the lake is the headwater of the Como Creek watershed and an ecologically sensitive habitat, per the City's Como Lake Park description as carried in park listings.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Blue Mountain Park's picnic area is bookable and large: City picnic listings set a 500-person maximum, with a fee for groups of 1 to 100 people and a damage deposit, for the 975 King Albert Avenue site.

The Rose Garden near this side of Coquitlam, at 624 Poirier Street, features over 800 roses with brick pathways and raised planters, per the City's picnic and outdoor spaces page — a Poirier Street amenity, not a Harbour Place park.
Como Lake's fish are a managed park feature: the City states the lake in Como Lake Park is stocked regularly in spring, with a fishing dock on the Lakeside Loop.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: costs and taxes

items.t: Coquitlam is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so a Harbour Place owner must complete the annual declaration.

The local cost check is park-adjacent, not a fee: Blue Mountain Park picnic rentals at 975 King Albert Avenue carry City rental fees and a damage deposit, which matters to a buyer planning large gatherings there, not to the house tax bill.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: getting around

items.t: Routes 156 and 157 also run Como Lake Avenue on the pocket's north side, per their TransLink timetables; no route is published on Baker Drive or King Albert Avenue themselves.
No SkyTrain station is in Harbour Place; buses on Como Lake Avenue and Austin Avenue connect to the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension stations in neighbouring areas.

blocks.text: Harbour Place: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood information at city scale: the City states Coquitlam River flood levels use the 200-year design flood and that dikes and pump stations protect low-lying properties, and Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 section 519 sets 30-metre and 15-metre watercourse setbacks.

Check Como Creek drainage for lots between Baker Drive and Como Lake: Como Lake is the headwater of the Como Creek watershed, so a lot draining toward the lake needs a City map check, not an assumption from its slope position.
Check slope lot by lot on King Albert Avenue at the foot of Blue Mountain: no City geotechnical page specific to Harbour Place was found, so no slope conclusion is stated here.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Harbour Place?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 7 houses listed in Harbour Place. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Harbour Place from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Harbour Place over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 2 sold.

faq.q: How big is Harbour Place compared with the rest of Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, Harbour Place held 1.9% of the 378 detached houses listed in Coquitlam.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Harbour Place than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses rose from 4 in June to 7 in October 2026 (+75.0%).

faq.q: What is in Blue Mountain Park, at 975 King Albert Avenue?
faq.a: Blue Mountain Park is this pocket's main park, at the foot of Blue Mountain on King Albert Avenue. The City lists a separate Blue Mountain Spray Park at the same 975 King Albert Avenue address, and City picnic listings for the park give a 500-person maximum capacity for its picnic area, with washrooms, water and electrical available with a rental.

faq.q: What can you do at Como Lake, just north of the houses?
faq.a: Como Lake Park, at 700 Gatensbury Street, offers the Lakeside Loop trail around the lake, a fishing dock and wetlands, and the City states the lake is stocked regularly in spring.

faq.q: Where do residents here swim indoors and borrow books?
faq.a: Poirier Sport and Leisure Complex, at 633 Poirier Street southwest of the pocket, is the nearest major City recreation complex in the City's facility listings. The nearest library branch is Coquitlam Public Library's Poirier Branch at 575 Poirier Street, not the City Centre Branch at 1169 Pinetree Way.

faq.q: Will Austin Avenue redevelopment change this neighbourhood?
faq.a: Areas east of Blue Mountain Street were kept out of the land-use changes, so a Baker Drive lot's designation must still be read lot by lot.

faq.q: What did houses in Harbour Place sell for?
faq.a: 7 houses sold in Harbour Place between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,000,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Harbour Place?
faq.a: The median was 25 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.9% of the last list price (14% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
